newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras hospital strike drags on after clashes.
newsitem.headline: Honduras hospital strike drags on after clashes.

text.p: A day after clashing with police, Honduran health workers pressed ahead on Thursday with a nine-day-old strike that has virtually paralysed hospitals.

About 10 protesters and five police were injured late on Wednesday when riot police firing tear gas clashed with workers who stormed the Health Ministry building and briefly held Health Minister Enrique Samayoa.
Police, who also fired into the air during the scuffle, dislodged some 300 protesters from the building and rescued Samayoa unharmed. On Thursday, armed riot police ringed the ministry building.
"We are still on strike and will not be intimidated by repressive acts by the government," Jose Baquedano, head of the National Medical Workers' Union, told Reuters.
The clashes were sparked by a warning on Wednesday that the government planned to fire workers who continued the strike.

Union leaders, government officials and business representatives met on Thursday in an attempt to stop the strike and end a recent spiral of labour unrest by public workers who want higher wages and cuts in the prices of public services.

The strike, branded "inhumane" by President Carlos Roberto Reina, has shut down some 28 hospitals and 500 health centres. Strikers have been treating only seriously ill patients and those already in hospitals.
